scope: Theorem 1.1 (A moment bound for every signed occurrence) of the manuscript “Signed tensor densities and diagram budgets for the Thorp shuffle” (preprints/Signed-tensor-densities-and-diagram-budgets-for-coordinate-sweeps-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 69f29b044ee825ef), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each sufficiently small fixed η̄ > 0, choose a sufficiently small κ̄ > 0 with κ̄ < η̄/256. There is an integer r ≥ 1, depending only on these fixed constants, such that for every d ≥ 1, every λ ⊢ n = 2d, and every occurrence (1), log(Dλ TrVλ (B∗ nBn)r ) ≤ ηdF(α, β) + gn(l), (3) where ηd = η̄ ( 1 − 1 2 √ d ) , κd = κ̄ ( 1 − 1 2 √ d ) , gn(l) = max{0, κdl log n − l log(n/l)}. Set gn(0) = 0 and interpret the logarithm of a zero trace as −∞.
